messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Re: Seeking Cool Shiny Examples
parts:
Hi Stephen,

I didn't actually compose a powerpoint or anything, I just went through the examples, and described how each of them brought something new to the table- such as their UI setup, use of d3 javascript, demonstration of basic statistical concepts, inclusion of a 'download' button, having action buttons to reduce server load, having one field impact the selections of other fields, etc. 

Also, its worth checking out the examples that googleVis has put together in conjunction with shiny, they are pretty neat.  Pageable tables seem to be the most practical application I have found from them so far, but the others look cooler.

Mike
